scenario: Retail chain HQ + store: POS isolation, cameras, guest, WAN.
prompt:
Business: 'Al-Noor Mart' — ek head office aur ek retail store.

Head office (Karachi):
- 6 office PCs (accounts + admin).
- Ek server jis par inventory system (HTTP) chale.

Retail store (Lahore):
- 2 POS terminals jo bilkul isolated honi chahiye (compliance).
- 1 back-office PC.
- 3 IP cameras jo store ke andar wired hon.
- Customer ke liye WiFi (guest).

Requirements:
- POS terminals apne alag network par hon, so that koi doosra device unhe na dekh sake.
- Cameras ka apna network ho.
- Guest WiFi sirf internet tak.
- Head office aur store aapas mein connected hon (static routing) so that inventory system dono jagah se open ho.
- Internet dono jagah chahiye (store ki alag line).
Exclusion: DHCP POS par nahi, and POS ke addresses static hon.
expected_behaviour: REFUSE-BY-NAME with three real reasons surfaced: (a) 'guest WiFi sirf internet tak' is a guest-isolation guarantee the engine refuses ('guest-isolation-unsupported'); (b) real IP cameras are not expressible — the schema's only IoT kind is smart_led, so the cameras cannot be built as asked; (c) 'internet dono jagah ... store ki alag line' over-claims — the engine builds one internet block at sites[0] (CG-3). The POS-static and two-site static-routing parts are otherwise buildable; the correct output names the three refusals rather than faking them.
why_valuable: The most enterprise-flavoured long document: multi-site retail with compliance-driven POS isolation. Held at the honest capability boundary (cameras + guest isolation) instead of faking support.
